Topics · Is there a God?

Can't the universe just exist for no reason?

All you can point to might not have been. An old argument: what has its being on loan, and does anything not?

Part 1 of 3

﴿كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ٢٦ وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلْجَلَـٰلِ وَٱلْإِكْرَامِ٢٧﴾

Translation of the meaning

Everyone upon it [i.e., the earth] will perish, And there will remain the Face[1597] of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.

Translator's notes

[1597] See footnote to 2:19.

Quran · Ar-Rahman 55:26-27

Translation

They will perish, but you will endure. Yes, all of them will wear out like a garment. You will change them like a cloak, and they will be changed. But you are the same. Your years will have no end.

Original · Hebrew

הֵ֤מָּה ׀ יֹאבֵדוּ֮ וְאַתָּ֪ה תַ֫עֲמֹ֥ד וְ֭כֻלָּם כַּבֶּ֣גֶד יִבְל֑וּ כַּלְּב֖וּשׁ תַּחֲלִיפֵ֣ם וְֽיַחֲלֹֽפוּ׃ וְאַתָּה־ה֑וּא וּ֝שְׁנוֹתֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א יִתָּֽמּוּ׃

the Psalms · 102:26-27

World English Bible

Look around the room. The chair, the building, the sun, you. Each is here, and each could have not been. None of them has to exist. Philosophers call such things contingent. In plain words, their existence is on loan: it does not come from what they are. Everything on earth, this passage says, passes, and one remains. The argument needs no claim about how the world began. It would hold even if the universe had always existed. It asks a different question: why is it there at all?

A question for you

Can you think of anything in the world that has to exist?

If you sayYes: energy, or the laws of nature.
ThenThen you have named a candidate for what does not borrow. The question is whether it could have been otherwise, and what kind of thing it would have to be.
If you sayNo. Everything could have been otherwise.
ThenThen you have granted the first step. The next part asks what follows.
If you sayThe question makes no sense.
ThenThat is a serious position in philosophy, and the next part states it at full strength.

Part 2 of 3

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ أَنتُمُ ٱلْفُقَرَآءُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَٱللَّهُ هُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ ٱلْحَمِيدُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O mankind, you are those in need of Allāh, while Allāh is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.

Quran · Fatir 35:15

Translation

The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands. He isn’t served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath and all things.

Original · Ancient Greek

ὁ θεὸς ὁ ποιήσας τὸν κόσμον καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ, οὗτος οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς ὑπάρχων κύριος οὐκ ἐν χειροποιήτοις ναοῖς κατοικεῖ οὐδὲ ὑπὸ χειρῶν ἀνθρωπίνων θεραπεύεται προσδεόμενός τινος, αὐτὸς διδοὺς πᾶσι ζωὴν καὶ πνοὴν καὶ τὰ πάντα·

Acts · 17:24-25

World English Bible

Now the strong reply. Russell said the universe is just there. Explain each part, said Hume, and you have explained the whole. Perhaps. But a thousand carriages do not move because each is pulled by the one before. If every member of a chain needs something outside itself, adding members does not remove the need. So either the whole is a brute fact, or something exists that does not borrow. This sentence names both poles: people in need, and God free of need.

A question for you

Which do you find easier to accept?

If you sayThe whole universe is a brute fact with no explanation.
ThenThat is a coherent choice, and honest thinkers make it. It means the deepest thing has no further reason.
If you saySomething exists that depends on nothing.
ThenThen you have reached the step that is hard to deny. Notice what you have not reached: that it knows, wills or cares. That is a further argument.
If you sayI do not think reason reaches this far.
ThenThat may be so. How far reason reaches is itself a live question.

Part 3 of 3

﴿ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Allāh, the Eternal Refuge.[2012]

Translator's notes

[2012] He who is absolute, perfect, complete, essential, self-sufficient and sufficient to meet the needs of all creation; the one eternally and constantly required and sought, depended upon by all existence and to whom all matters will ultimately return.

Quran · Al-Ikhlas 112:2

Translation

Now therefore, Yahweh our God, save us, I beg you, out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, Yahweh, are God alone.”

Original · Hebrew

וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֥נוּ נָ֖א מִיָּד֑וֹ וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י אַתָּ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃

2 Kings · 19:19

World English Bible

What has this reached, if it holds? Something that exists by itself, depends on nothing, and on which other things depend. It could not be made of parts, since it would then depend on them. It could not be one more thing in the universe. That is all the argument gives: a Source. It shows no person, no mercy and no message. Those need other reasons. This sentence gives it one rare word, which commentators explain as the One to whom all turn in need.

A question for you

What has this argument not yet shown you?

If you sayThat the Source is one.
ThenThat has its own question, which starts from the order of the world.
If you sayThat it knows or cares.
ThenThat is the question most people care about, and it needs more than this argument.
If you sayThat any of this matters to my life.
ThenA fair question. A bare argument rarely answers it.
